# ADR-024: Ubiquitous language for the execution model

## Decision

### Cluster authority is exercised through a per-cluster agent (amendment 2026-08-24)

The callers keep their behaviour, not just their shape. A CR that no longer
exists is an ordinary answer and stops the work; anything else throws so the
caller retries rather than treating a denial as an absence — the distinction the
Floor used to make by sniffing a 404 out of a Kubernetes error, and the reason
`found:false` is served at 200.

*Amended 2026-08-29: the `kubernetes.agent` handler is no longer one of these
callers. It used to re-GET the terminal CR before processing it, which silently
scoped settling a run to the one cluster this Floor can reach; it now settles
from the event's own report, which carries the full status. Th…

# Feature Specification: Running Stations in Any Kubernetes Cluster

## FR8 — Live telemetry from a satellite

### FR8.1 — Relaying telemetry through the cluster-agent *(added 2026-08-28)*

Posting straight to the public sink works, and loses a batch to any blip: a run
pod has no queue and makes no second attempt. A satellite may instead point its
pods at its OWN cluster-agent, which forwards the batch through the same event
proxy everything else in that cluster reports through.

## Problem Statement

The groundwork for lifting this exists. ADR-044 extracted **cluster-agent** as
the only process holding a Kubernetes client, one per cluster, reporting
terminal Agent CR phases inward over HTTP through the event-router's
`POST /api/events` front door — recorded explicitly as "what allows more than
one execution cluster". `HttpEventReporter`
(`libs/shared/src/outbound/project/events/event-reporter-http.ts`) exists precisely so
a producer can report from somewhere the database does not reach (its header
comment is corrected in this change to name the satellite cluster-agent this
spec defines, rather than the satellite Floor it predates). What is missing is
the registry (which clusters exist), the capab…

- `outbound/cluster/`: the HTTP client to the cluster agent, the Agent-CR backend and their ports.
- `outbound/project/cluster-agents/`: the registry adapters, capacity and tag rules, the per-agent token.
- In `outbound/project/agents/`: the CRD rendering for the catalog sync (`agent-crd`), the catalog-events and catalog-status adapters, and the agent runner chain behind `project.agents` (`agent-runner`, `station-port`, `k8s-port`, `station-credentials`, `claude-cli`, `llm-port`). Nothing outside `libs/shared` called `project.agents`, so the getter and its providers go from the Project facade too.
- The `kubernetes.agent*` event mapping, `kube-config`, the pod-failure and Kubernetes error helpers, `poll-loop`, `launch-release`, the run-credential signer, `registry-or-shared-token`.

Worth a `kubectl get agents -n ai-agents | wc -l` before assuming this is theoretical. The new Role grants both verbs.

## What Changed

**`apps/cluster-agent`** — 12 domain operations under `/api/cluster`, bearer-authed, **no `pg` dependency at all**.

Three of the underlying interactions are **read-modify-write pairs** — the status subresource, the Secret key with its 5× 409 retry, the catalog create-409-replace. content.text: {"answer": "Agent pods (the agent/station pods, driven by the ai-agent-subsystem controller and its Agent CRDs) run in Kubernetes clusters, which can be more than one. Lore's main Floor app does not hold a Kubernetes client for them. Under ADR-044, the separate `cluster-agent` process is the only one that holds a Kubernetes client. There is one cluster-agent per cluster. Lore reaches it over an HTTP API (`/api/cluster`, bearer-authed). The cluster-agent reports terminal Agent CR phases back through the event-router's `POST /api/events`. This is what allows more than one execution cluster. One caveat: issue 891 describes an earlier state in which the Floor used `@kubernetes/client-node` with `loadFromCluster()` at six sites. The later cluster-agent work (PR 1482, PR 2484, ADR-024 amendment) moved that cluster access into the cluster-agent. I did not check whether any direct client use remains in the code.", "sources": ["specs/running-stations-in-any-k8s-cluster/spec.md", "adrs/ADR-024-ubiquitous-language-execution-model.md", "pull-1482", "pull-2484", "issue-891"]}
